question: According to the European Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Drug Addiction, fentanyl use across the EU has been on the rise in recent years thanks to its ease of production and distribution. Originally developed to relieve pain in cancer patients, fentanyl is widely used as a narcotic: it is 100 times stronger than morphine and 50 times stronger than heroine. In view of this: What preventive steps will it take to curb fentanyl use?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.5.2024) The EU Drugs Strategy 2021-20251 and action plan2 identify the priorities for the EU drug policy. Their implementation is a joint effort notably by the Commission and Member States to continue to reduce drug-related deaths and non-fatal overdoses, for example by increasing the availability of take-home naloxone programmes.

The Commission works closely with its agencies, in particular the European Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Drug Addiction (EMCDDA) and the European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol), to monitor the situation of synthetic drugs across the EU, including fentanyl.

With the revision of the EMCDDA mandate3, the agency will strengthen its threat assessment capabilities to look into developments that negatively impact health, safety and security and will develop a European drug alert system to facilitate the exchange of information on developments requiring rapid actions to safeguard health, social aspects, safety and security.

Furthermore, the Commission adopted on 18 October 2023 an EU roadmap to fight drug trafficking and organised crime4. The roadmap confirmed the EU’s active engagement in the global coalition to address synthetic drug threats, launched by the United States and pointed to the holding of further exchanges with China to boost cooperation in this area.
